rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. Testing RNA-only with PCA encoding and singleprofile isolates the RNA modality's performance, providing a reference point to compare against multimodal or image-only approaches later. This clarifies the baseline accuracy and helps prioritize subsequent experiments on critical design choices like fusion or aggregation.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile RNA-only with PCA and avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration by testing a key design choice (multiprofile) while keeping RNA encoder consistent, providing critical insight into whether multiprofile improves performance without overcomplicating the model.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002, 0.5907 accuracy) outperform singleprofile models. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It directly extends the promising multiprofile direction while minimizing changes to other design choices, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (0.59 vs 0.48). This experiment tests whether replacing PCA with scvi_n200 RNA encoder (a more sophisticated representation) maintains the multiprofile advantage. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while keeping aggregation method (avgpool) consistent with the current best, addressing key uncertainty about representation quality.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.650124). This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation instead of avgpool (used in config_005) further improves performance with the same scvi_n200 encoder. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, which is critical for understanding model behavior, and builds on the promising scvi_n200 encoder choice.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only with multiprofile and scvi_n200 RNA encoder achieves the highest accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests combining this strong RNA encoder with image data (resnet50) using avgpool aggregation (mirroring the top rna_only setup) and concat fusion. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches can improve accuracy further by isolating the effect of image modality and fusion strategy.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.653 accuracy) are strong. This experiment tests whether adding multimodal data (resnet50 image encoder) with the same transformer aggregation and concat fusion can further improve performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal integration while building on the successful RNA encoder and aggregation method, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of multimodal benefits.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 encoders, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (config_032, 0.6878 accuracy) are strong. This experiment tests replacing concat fusion with weighted fusion to isolate its impact on performance. It directly builds on the current top performer, addressing a key design choice with minimal changes, and could either confirm or improve upon the existing leading configuration under the limited budget.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) in the same multimodal setup could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice while maintaining the proven effective aggregation and fusion strategies, balancing exploitation of current best practices with exploration of potential improvements.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_033) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests if replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (a stronger baseline) maintains or improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder. It is the best use of the last experiment as it directly addresses a critical design choice with high potential to improve accuracy.
